_about: The one list of position relations every mode uses (Find it, Tidy up, Monsoon rush, Snap, the clinic's courtyard). Read by js/shared/rel.js; the spec is docs/shared-api.md section 1. A relation id is what scene spots and rows carry; its word is the phrase the child hears. NO relation has Kutchi yet (Questions for Mum, section on positions): every word below is an English placeholder with kutchi null, shown grey like any other placeholder, and swapped by data when the family answers. kind: 'anchor' needs an anchor (a scene anchor, a person, or a placed item: 'in the bowl', 'next to the plate'); 'unary' needs none ('in the middle'); 'leave' is Tidy up's 'leave it where it is'. derived: how rel.js decides it between two spots when the anchor is a placed item rather than scenery (neighbour graph, never free geometry). frame 'player': left and right are the player's, as seen on screen. cams: which scene cameras (T top-down, H high angle, E eye level) can show it honestly. order: the acquisition order (in, on, under, behind, next to, in front of, between), used by generators to introduce one at a time.

aliases._about: Other spellings the mode designs used, mapped to the one id. rel.js normalises through this, so old data keeps working.

grammar._about: Where the position goes in a row, as word slots: x = the thing, anchor = what it's by, rel = the relation word, anchor2 = the second anchor of 'between'. Kutchi puts the position after the noun (a postposition), so the placeholder order is {x} {anchor} {rel}. Until the family says whether the anchor changes shape ('table-ni niche'), each (anchor, relation) pair is recorded as one phrase (a phrase word id in the mode's data wins over building it).

words._about: Placeholder words for Cook.data.words (merge with Rel.mergeWords). kutchi null = placeholder, shown grey.
